verses.zh: （ 大 衛 的 詩 ， 交 與 伶 長 。 用 絲 弦 的 樂 器 ， 調 用 第 八 。 ） 耶 和 華 啊 ， 求 你 不 要 在 怒 中 責 備 我 ， 也 不 要 在 烈 怒 中 懲 罰 我 ！
verses.en: For the music director, to be accompanied by stringed instruments, according to the sheminith style;[NOTE:1] a psalm of David.Lord, do not rebuke me in your anger.Do not discipline me in your raging fury.[NOTE:2]
notes: Psalm 6. The psalmist begs the Lord to withdraw his anger and spare his life. Having received a positive response to his prayer, the psalmist then confronts his enemies and describes how they retreat.
The meaning of the Hebrew term שְׁמִינִית (sheminit, “sheminith”) is uncertain; perhaps it refers to a particular style of music. See 1 Chr 15:21.

verses.zh: 耶 和 華 啊 ， 求 你 可 憐 我 ， 因 為 我 軟 弱 。 耶 和 華 啊 ， 求 你 醫 治 我 ， 因 為 我 的 骨 頭 發 戰 。
verses.en: Have mercy on me,[NOTE:1] Lord, for I am frail.Heal me, Lord, for my bones are shaking.[NOTE:2]
notes: The implication is that the psalmist has sinned, causing God to discipline him by bringing a life-threatening illness upon him (see vv. 2-7).
Or “show me favor.”

verses.zh: 我 心 也 大 大 地 驚 惶 。 耶 和 華 啊 ， 你 要 到 幾 時 才 救 我 呢 ？
verses.en: I am absolutely terrified,[NOTE:1] and you, Lord—how long will this continue?[NOTE:2]
notes: Normally the verb בָּהַל (bahal) refers to an emotional response and means “tremble with fear, be terrified” (see vv. 3, 10). Perhaps here the “bones” are viewed as the seat of the psalmist’s emotions. However, the verb may describe one of the effects of his physical ailment, perhaps a fever. In Ezek 7:27 the verb describes how the hands of the people will shake with fear when they experience the horrors of divine judgment.
Heb “my being is very terrified.” The suffixed form of נֶפֶשׁ (nefesh, “being”) is often equivalent to a pronoun in poetic texts.

verses.zh: 耶 和 華 啊 ， 求 你 轉 回 搭 救 我 ！ 因 你 的 慈 愛 拯 救 我 。
verses.en: Relent, Lord, rescue me![NOTE:1] Deliver me because of your faithfulness.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and you, Lord, how long?” The suffering psalmist speaks in broken syntax. He addresses God, but then simply cries out with a brief, but poignant, question: How long will this (= his suffering) continue?
Heb “my being,” or “my life.” The suffixed form of נֶפֶשׁ (nefesh, “being”) is often equivalent to a pronoun in poetic texts.

verses.zh: 因 為 ， 在 死 地 無 人 記 念 你 ， 在 陰 間 有 誰 稱 謝 你 ？
verses.en: For no one remembers you in the realm of death.[NOTE:1] In Sheol who gives you thanks?[NOTE:2]
notes: Deliver me because of your faithfulness. Though the psalmist is experiencing divine discipline, he realizes that God has made a commitment to him in the past, so he appeals to God’s faithfulness in his request for help.

Heb “for there is not in death your remembrance.” The Hebrew noun זֵכֶר (zekher, “remembrance”) here refers to the name of the Lord as invoked in liturgy and praise. Cf. Pss 30:4; 97:12. “Death” here refers to the realm of death where the dead reside. See the reference to Sheol in the next line.

verses.zh: 我 因 唉 哼 而 困 乏 ； 我 每 夜 流 淚 ， 把 床 榻 漂 起 ， 把 褥 子 濕 透 。
verses.en: I am exhausted as I groan.All night long I drench my bed in tears;[NOTE:1] my tears saturate the cushion beneath me.[NOTE:2]
notes: The rhetorical question anticipates the answer, “no one.”sn In Sheol who gives you thanks? According to the OT, those who descend into the realm of death/Sheol are cut off from God’s mighty deeds and from the worshiping covenant community that experiences divine intervention (Pss 30:9; 88:10-12; Isa 38:18). In his effort to elicit a positive divine response, the psalmist reminds God that he will receive no praise or glory if he allows the psalmist to die. Dead men do not praise God!
Heb “I cause to swim through all the night my bed.”

verses.zh: 我 因 憂 愁 眼 睛 乾 癟 ， 又 因 我 一 切 的 敵 人 眼 睛 昏 花 。
verses.en: My eyes[NOTE:1] grow dim[NOTE:2] from suffering;they grow weak[NOTE:3] because of all my enemies.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “with my tears my bed I flood/melt.”
The Hebrew text has the singular “eye” here.
Or perhaps, “are swollen.”
Or perhaps, “grow old.”

verses.zh: 你 們 一 切 作 孽 的 人 ， 離 開 我 罷 ！ 因 為 耶 和 華 聽 了 我 哀 哭 的 聲 音 。
verses.en: Turn back from me, all you who behave wickedly,[NOTE:1] for the Lord has heard the sound of my weeping.[NOTE:2]
notes: In his weakened condition the psalmist is vulnerable to the taunts and threats of his enemies.
Heb “all [you] workers of wickedness.” See Ps 5:5.

verses.zh: 耶 和 華 聽 了 我 的 懇 求 ； 耶 和 華 必 收 納 我 的 禱 告 。
verses.en: The Lord has heard my appeal for mercy;the Lord has accepted[NOTE:1] my prayer.
notes: The Lord has heard. The psalmist’s mood abruptly changes because the Lord responded positively to the lament and petition of vv. 1-7 and promised him deliverance.

verses.zh: 我 的 一 切 仇 敵 都 必 羞 愧 ， 大 大 驚 惶 ； 他 們 必 要 退 後 ， 忽 然 羞 愧 。
verses.en: They will be humiliated[NOTE:1] and absolutely terrified.[NOTE:2] All my enemies will turn back and be suddenly humiliated.
notes: The prefixed verbal form is probably a preterite here; it is parallel to a perfect and refers to the fact that the Lord has responded favorably to the psalmist’s request.

In the structure of the Psalm, this verse is either another petition or a statement of confidence. If a petition, the four prefixed verbal forms in this verse should be understood as jussives. By form, many prefixed verbs can be either imperfect or jussive. But the third verb in the series, יָשֻׁבוּ (yashuvu), can be distinguished as an imperfect by its qibbuts theme vowel, and is not a jussive (which would have had a qamets hatuph or holem). Expecting all four verbs to be the same due to parallelism leads to the conclusion that this section is a statement of confidence, in which the imperfect verbs should be treated as future.
